title: Gold & Silver Drop: Weighing US-Iran Deal Prospects
description: Global gold prices dropped by $81/oz and silver by $3/oz on May 27, reacting to potential de-escalation in US-Iran tensions. Precious metals typically act as .

faq.q: Why did gold and silver prices drop suddenly?
faq.a: Gold and silver prices dropped primarily due to prospects of a potential de-escalation in tensions between the US and Iran. As safe-haven assets, their demand tends to decrease when geopolitical risks are perceived to lessen.

faq.q: Does this mean gold is no longer a good investment?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Gold remains a valuable asset for portfolio diversification, acting as a hedge against inflation and currency depreciation over the long term. Short-term fluctuations are common and do not negate its long-term utility.

faq.q: How does the US-Iran deal affect Indian gold prices?
faq.a: Indian gold prices are directly influenced by international COMEX prices. A drop in global prices typically translates into lower domestic prices, adjusted for the rupee-dollar exchange rate and import duties.

faq.q: Should I sell my gold holdings now?
faq.a: Selling decisions should align with your personal financial goals and asset allocation strategy, not just short-term market movements. Consult a financial advisor before making significant changes to your portfolio.

faq.q: What role do interest rates play in gold prices?
faq.a: Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like gold, making fixed-income investments more attractive. Conversely, lower rates can boost gold's appeal.

faq.q: Is silver more volatile than gold?
faq.a: Yes, silver typically exhibits higher volatility than gold. This is due to its dual nature as both a safe-haven asset and an industrial metal, making it sensitive to both geopolitical events and economic growth prospects.

faq.q: How can I invest in gold in India?
faq.a: Indian investors can buy physical gold (jewellery, coins, bars), invest in Gold Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), or purchase Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) offered by the government.
